{{short description|Russian chemist of ethnic Tatar origin (born 1935)}}{{Family name hatnote|Sultanovich|Mirzayanov|lang=Eastern Slavic}}

'''Vil Sultanovich Mirzayanov'''  ({{langx|ru|Вил Султанович Мирзаянов}}, {{langx|tt-Cyrl|Вил Солтан улы Мирзаҗанов}}) is a [[Russian people|Russian]] [[chemist]] of ethnic [[Tatars|Tatar]] origin{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}} who now lives in the [[United States]], best known for revealing secret [[chemical weapon]]s experimentation in Russia.

==Early life==
Vil Sultanovich Mirzayanov was born in a village in rural Bashkortostan, the son of the village school teacher. The Mirzayanov family is [[Tatars|Tatar]], a [[Turkic peoples|Turkic]] ethnic minority in Russia.{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}} His father, a staunch [[Communism|Communist]], broke with a 200 year old family tradition in which the oldest sons entered the [[Muslim clergy]].<ref>[https://outskirtspress.com/StateSecrets_aninsiderschronicle State Secrets - About the Author - Biography of Dr. Vil Mirzayanov], ''outskirtspress.com''</ref> In 1953, he graduated from the Dyurtyuli Tatar School No. 1 with a silver medal.

==Career==
Mirzayanov was employed by the State Research Institute of Organic Chemistry and Technology. He was then assigned to a secret military chemical weapons laboratory, [[GosNIIOKhT]] ({{Langx|ru|ГосНИИОХТ}}) situated in [[Shikhany]], which was developing the [[Novichok agent]] programme of nerve agents. He was head of a counter-intelligence department that performed measurements outside the chemical weapons facilities to make sure that foreign spies could not detect any traces of production. To his horror, the levels of deadly substances were 80 times greater than the maximum safe concentration.<ref name="Albats">[[Yevgenia Albats]] and Catherine A. Fitzpatrick. ''The State Within a State: The KGB and Its Hold on Russia&nbsp;— Past, Present, and Future'', 1994. {{ISBN|0-374-18104-7}} (see pages 325-328)</ref> (A full account by Mirzayanov is available online.<ref name="Vil">{{cite web | url=http://www.stimson.org/images/uploads/research-pdfs/Report17.pdf | title=Chemical Weapons Disarmament in Russia: Problems and Prospects; Dismantling the Soviet/Russian Chemical Weapons Complex: An Insider's View | publisher=Henry L. Stimson Center, Washington, D.C. | date=17 October 1995 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150824060701/http://www.stimson.org/images/uploads/research-pdfs/Report17.pdf | archive-date=August 24, 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref>)

Concerned mostly with environmental contamination, Mirzayanov and his colleague [[Lev Alexandrovich Fyodorov|Lev Fyodorov]] decided to reveal the extent of chemical weapons experimentation in Russia, which Russia used as a workaround to comply with the proposed [[1990 Chemical Weapons Accord]] and the existing [[Wyoming Memorandum of Understanding]] but still produce chemical-like weapons. In 1992, they published an article about the USSR and Russia's development of extremely potent fourth-generation chemical weapons from the 1970s until the early 1990s, in ''[[Moskovskiye Novosti]]'' weekly,<ref>{{Cite book|title=Ciottone's Disaster Medicine|edition=Second|year=2016|pages=489–498|chapter=Future Biological and Chemical Weapons|editor-first=Gregory R.|editor-last=Ciottone|first1=Robert G.|last1=Darling|first2=Erin E.|last2=Noste|doi=10.1016/B978-0-323-28665-7.00080-7|publisher=Elsevier|location=Amsterdam|isbn=9780323286657|s2cid=132183263 }}</ref><ref>Lev Fyodorov and Vil Mirzayanov, "Poisoned Politics," ''[[Moskovskiye Novosti]]'' weekly No. 39, 1992.  Much of this information was published earlier in the newspaper "Top Secret" run by [[Artyom Borovik]] in September 1991. However the KGB did not arrest Mirzayanov earlier due to political turmoil in Russia at this time, according to a book by [[Yevgenia Albats]].</ref> and for safety purposes in the [[Baltimore Sun]] through an associated article written by veteran correspondent [[Will Englund]].<ref name=BSun1992260123>{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/1992/09/16/ex-soviet-scientist-says-gorbachevs-regime-created-new-nerve-gas-in-91/|title=Ex-Soviet scientist says Gorbachev's regime created new nerve gas in '91|date=September 16, 1992|publisher=Baltimore Sun|author=Will Englund|access-date=March 12, 2018}}</ref><ref name=WPost5002be4fe1ee>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2018/03/12/what-is-novichok-the-russian-nerve-agent-and-the-scientist-who-revealed-it/|title=What a brave Russian scientist told me about Novichok, the nerve agent identified in the spy attack|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|author=Will Englund|author-link=Will Englund|date= March 12, 2018|access-date=March 12, 2018}}</ref> The publication appeared just on the eve of Russia's signing of the 1990 Chemical Weapons Convention. Later according to Mirzayanov, the Russian Military Chemical Complex (MCC) was using defense conversion money received from the West for development of the chemical warfare facility.<ref name="Birstein">Vadim J. Birstein. ''The Perversion Of Knowledge: The True Story of Soviet Science.'' Westview Press (2004) {{ISBN|0-8133-4280-5}}</ref><ref name="Albats"/>

==Exposing Russian secrets==
Mirzayanov was arrested on October 22, 1992, on charges of [[treason]], brought by the Russian [[military industrial complex]] authorities — he was not allowed to know the exact charges, as they were also declared a state secret. Held in [[Lefortovo Prison]], during the resultant court case, the existence of Novichok agents was openly admitted by Russian authorities. According to expert witness testimonies prepared for the [[KGB]] by three scientists, Novichok and other related chemical agents had indeed been produced and therefore the disclosure by Mirzayanov represented [[high treason]].<ref>"the talk [by Mirzayanov] about binary weapons was no more than a verbal construct, an argument ex adverso, and only the MCC [Russian Military Chemical Complex] could corroborate or refute this natural assumption.  By entangling V. S. Mirzayanov in investigation, the MCC confirmed the stated hypothesis, advancing it to the ranks of proven facts." [http://www.fas.org/nuke/guide/russia/cbw/jptac008_l94001.htm Chemical Weapons in Russia: History, Ecology, Politics] ''www.fas.org'', accessed 9 October 2020</ref>

However, the trial collapsed. Mirzayanov was released because "not one of the formulas or names of poisonous substances in the ''Moscow News'' article was new to the Soviet press, nor were locations ... of testing sites revealed."<ref name="Albats"/> According to [[Yevgenia Albats]], "the real [[Classified information|state secret]] revealed by Fyodorov and Mirzayanov was that generals had lied&nbsp;— and were still lying&nbsp;— to both the international community and their fellow citizens."<ref name="Albats"/>

Mirzayanov was released, but kept under house arrest and observation. In 1995, he relocated to the United States where he presently resides,<ref name="Hoffman">{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/inatl/longterm/coldwar/wasteside1.htm |title=Wastes of War: Soviets Reportedly Built Weapon Despite Pact |author=David Hoffman |date=August 16, 1998 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=2007-07-20}}</ref> taking a position at [[Rutgers University]] in [[New Jersey]].<ref name=WPost5002be4fe1ee/>

On October 26, 2008, Mirzayanov was elected to the Presidium of the [[Mejlis|Milli Mejlis]] of the [[Tatarstan|Tatar People]] in exile.<ref>[https://www.azatliq.org/a/1333009.html Мирзаянов Милли Мәҗлеснең Баш нәзире итеп сайланды] ''tr. Mirzayanov was elected Prime Minister of the National Assembly'', ''azatliq.org''</ref> On January 17, 2009, in an article on [[CNN]], he published the DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE OF TATARSTAN, adopted at a Special Meeting of the Milli Mejlis of the Tatar People on December 20, 2008.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140330111914/http://ireport.cnn.com/docs/DOC-183351 THE DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE OF TATARSTAN], ''cnn.com'', January 17, 2009</ref> At a conference on the separation of Tatarstan from Russia, held in Ankara in the same year, Mirzayanov was elected "Prime Minister" of the "[[government in exile]]". In March 2010, Mirzayanov signed the "[[Putin Must Go]]" campaign.<ref>[http://stuki-druki.com/authors/Mirzayanov-Vil.php Вил Мирзаянов - биография], ''stuki-druki.com'' (Biography in Russian including some images)</ref>

In March 2018, after the [[poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]], Mirzayanov spoke about how Russia maintained tight control over its Novichok stockpile and that the agent is too complicated for a non-state actor to have weaponized. "It's torture. It's absolutely incurable." "I never imagined even in my bad dreams that this chemical weapon, developed with my participation, would be used as terrorist weapons."<ref name="2018-03-14_ABC">[http://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-03-14/only-russia-could-be-behind-uk-poison-attack-toxin-inventor-says/9546298 Novichok nerve agent inventor says only Russia could be behind UK poison attack]. [[Reuters]]/[[Associated Press|AP]], ''[[ABC News Online]]'', 2018-03-14</ref> Both victims later recovered and left the hospital.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-britain-russia-skripal-hospital/poisoned-russian-agent-sergei-skripal-recovering-rapidly-hospital-says-idUKKCN1HD1PJ|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180407124944/https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-britain-russia-skripal-hospital/poisoned-russian-agent-sergei-skripal-recovering-rapidly-hospital-says-idUKKCN1HD1PJ|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 7, 2018|title=Poisoned Russian agent Sergei Skripal recovering rapidly, hospital says|last=Alistair Smout|first=Guy Faulconbridge|date=7 April 2018|work=Reuters.|access-date=11 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-44165718|title=Ex-spy Sergei Skripal discharged after poisoning|last=Nathoo|first=Leila|date=18 May 2018|work=BBC News|access-date=11 July 2018}}</ref> Mirzayanov said only the Russians can be behind the weapon's use in the poisoning and said he was convinced Russia carried it out as a way of intimidating opponents of President Vladimir Putin.<ref name="itstherussian" >[https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/its-the-russians-says-chemist-who-uncovered-existence-of-novichok-1823733 It's The Russians, Says Chemist Who Uncovered Existence Of 'Novichok']. ''NDTV''. 14 March 2018. Retrieved 21 August 2018.</ref> He added that the Russians could argue that maybe someone had synthesized them "and they could make me guilty!"<ref name="itstherussian" />
